Independent School of the Year
Berkhampstead is a happy, non-selective school; we pride ourselves on the breadth of our curriculum and our nurturing and inclusive ethos. pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head of School
At Berkhampstead, we see every child as an individual, each with their own unique spark, interests and potential. Our job - and our joy - is to recognise and nurture this individuality, offering a tailored education within a warm, inclusive and caring environment.
We are a non-selective independent day school, but that doesn’t mean we compromise on ambition. High standards and a love of learning run through everything we do. With small class sizes and an exceptional teaching team, every child is known, supported and stretched – and this personalised approach leads to excellent 11+ and scholarship outcomes.
From their very first days in Kindergarten, our pupils are taught by subject specialists who bring real depth, rigour and passion to their teaching. This expert input allows children to thrive in a stimulating environment that stretches their thinking and builds lasting confidence.
But a Berkhampstead education is about so much more than just academic results. We offer a rich and rounded experience – one where music, sport, drama and outdoor learning play a central role. Our pupils are curious, enthusiastic and full of life. They leave us not just well-prepared for senior school, but as resilient, confident and kind young people, ready to embrace the world.
We were proud that our excellent pastoral care and ambitious curriculum were recognised in our most recent ISI inspection, with inspectors praising our pupils’ independence, positive attitudes and enthusiasm for learning.Set in the beautiful, leafy surroundings of Pittville Circus in Cheltenham, Berkhampstead is a joyful, vibrant school – a place where childhood is celebrated and curiosity is encouraged every step of the way.

“My own family is very important to me, and I see the Berkhampstead community as an extension of this. This is a very special place, and I am proud to be its Head of School.” Mrs Michelle Bareham
OUR AIMS
“The happy, caring and fun environment is met through robust pastoral systems and a clear culture of care, which promotes pupils’ self-knowledge, self-esteem and self-confidence.” ISI Report, November 2023

pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care & Holiday Club
We understand that family life is busy – and we’re here to help. Our wraparound care and Holiday Club give parents the reassurance that their child is happy, safe and well looked after beyond the school day.
Wraparound Care
For parents who need an early drop off, Breakfast Club provides a calm and sociable start to the day. A healthy breakfast is served, including fruit, yoghurt, toast and cereal.
After-School Club 3.30pm – 5.30pm
After school, children can enjoy a varied programme that combines activities, relaxation and homework support. A light afternoon tea is served at 4.30pm, and children can stay until 5.30pm.
Our after-school and lunchtime clubs are diverse and engaging, allowing children to explore interests beyond the classroom. Options range from sport, gardening and music, to cycling proficiency, chess and even Mandarin. This enriching co-curricular offering helps children to develop new skills, build confidence and have fun with friends in a relaxed and familiar environment.
Book Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care Fees
“Pupils benefit from a broad and interesting activity programme, which enables them to deepen their knowledge, skills and understanding whilst gaining independence and developing skills for life.” ISI Report, November 2023
Holiday Club & Berky Experience Club
Available every school holiday (except the final week of December) for children aged 3–8. Activities include arts and crafts, cookery, music, sport, drama and lots of outdoor play.
Berky Experience Days - ages 7 to 11
Available for older pupils (Years 3–6) run on selected days during the holidays. These specialist sessions offer engaging, age-appropriate opportunities such as chess, baking, art, creative writing, sport and grammar school preparation.
Please contact holidayclub@berkhampsteadschool.co.uk if you have any questions.

Creative Arts
At Berkhampstead, the creative arts lie at the heart of school life, inspiring a love of self-expression from the very earliest years.
MUSIC & PERFORMING ARTS
Music and performance flourish across the school. From Pre-Prep music groups to at least nine Prep School ensembles, every child can experience the joy of making music together. From Year 3, pupils can take private lessons in over 13 instruments with our visiting music teachers.
Performance is central to school life; recitals, nativities, carol services, and our annual Spring Concerts at Cheltenham Town Hall give pupils plenty of opportunities to shine. Drama is equally valued, with our LAMDA-trained drama teacher supporting acting, storytelling, and public speaking and singing. Many pupils go on to achieve music and drama scholarships to senior schools, reflecting the strength of our creative arts provision.
ART
From Kindergarten, children are encouraged to explore ideas freely and develop their own creative voice. Our art rooms provide the perfect space to experiment with a wide range of materials and techniques. From Year 3, our specialist art teacher ensures skills and artistic expression are honed with depth and expertise.
Pupils experience a rich and varied curriculum, including both two- and three-dimensional work. Year 6 enjoy annual visiting artist workshops, with recent sessions in willow sculpture, mosaic, and screen printing. Every child’s creativity is celebrated in our own Summer Art Exhibition, and our pupils also shine annually at the Malvern St James Primary School Art Exhibition. Many of our pupils go on to earn art scholarships to senior schools, reflecting both their talent and our specialist teaching.

Superb Grammar and Senior School Preparation
From age 7 (Year 3), all children take part in weekly dedicated critical thinking lessons - an excellent foundation for grammar school entrance tests and a powerful tool for developing reasoning, logic and verbal skills.
There is also a heavy focus on Maths and English within our weekly timetable across all year groups, and these subjects are taught by dedicated and experienced subject specialist teachers. Children with a broad vocabulary, strong comprehension and developed maths reasoning skills usually perform better.

Our critical thinking lessons and workshops are delivered by teachers with a wealth of experience and an impressive track record of success in preparing children for grammar school entrance tests.
Our careful, personalised preparation leads to outstanding results. We are proud of our strong track record of grammar school places and scholarships awarded in academics, sport, music, art and drama.

Berky Gets Greener
Environmental commitment has always been at the heart of Berkhampstead, and in 2019, we launched 'Berky Gets Greener' - a dedicated movement focused on protecting and preserving the environment.
Berky Eco-committees: Making a Difference
At Berkhampstead, our commitment to the environment is driven by our two Eco-Committees - one in the Prep School and one in the Pre-Prep. These committees, made up of representatives from each class, work tirelessly to promote the careful use of our planet’s resources in school, at home and within the local community.
We were incredibly proud to achieve the Eco-Schools Green Flag Award with Distinction in the Summer Term 2025. This prestigious recognition reflects the dedication of our pupils and staff and was awarded in part thanks to key initiatives such as promoting sustainable travel, planting 37 mature trees in the Pre-Prep playground, installing an EV charger, increasing bike rack provision, conducting a whole-school traffic survey and introducing a robust anti-idling policy.
Our passionate eco-warriors have also spearheaded numerous other green initiatives, including the installation of motion-sensor lights, the recycling of crisp packets, medicine blister packs and batteries, and improving paper recycling across the school. They are often seen armed with litter pickers, keeping our school grounds clean, and they enthusiastically contribute to school events, such as growing plants to sell at the Summer Festival.We encourage all our pupils to lead greener lifestyles through the Berky Eco Pledge. Prep School children are challenged to complete five of the ten pledges, while Pre-Prep children aim to fulfil three from a simplified version. Central to this effort is the expectation for every child to “Spread the Word!” about sustainable living.
The pledge allows pupils to showcase their commitment to the environment through pictures and writing. Those who successfully complete it are awarded a smart Eco-Warrior badge to wear on their blazers.

Superb Early Years Provision
At Berkhampstead School, we believe these early years are precious. They lay the foundations not only for academic success, but for gently fostering confidence and character.
In our Kindergarten and Reception classes, children are nurtured and inspired from the beginning of their educational journey.
“Research consistently shows that the greatest educational impact comes from investment in the earliest years, when children’s brains, confidence and learning habits develop most rapidly.”
DfE; Public Health England; Education Endowment Foundation.
Our children benefit from specialist teaching in French, Music and PE.
These passionate subject experts bring depth of knowledge and enthusiasm to every lesson, igniting curiosity and helping children to begin building firm foundations in their learning.
The children learn in bright, modern classrooms and enjoy access to an all-weather games area, a newly constructed playground, a dedicated Early Years gym, a Forest School area and a wealth of high-quality resources.
Reception Timetable 2026-27

A strong academic foundation begins early; from Kindergarten we use the Essential Letters and Sounds phonics programme to gently begin the process of developing fluent, confident readers and writers, alongside White Rose Maths to support a carefully structured and engaging approach to mathematics.
Each day, our children enjoy delicious, home cooked lunches served in a family-style setting, with a member of staff leading each table to encourage healthy eating habits and good table manners. Our smart school uniform fosters a strong sense of belonging, while thoughtful, considerate behaviour is woven into everyday life.
From their very first days at Berkhampstead, our Early Years children are encouraged to explore, question and discover - building a firm educational foundation, rooted in confidence and a genuine love of learning.

Our History
Berkhampstead School has been educating children for over 80 years. Central to our ethos is that happy children achieve remarkable things.
The Beginning
In 1945, Mrs Edna Andrews, a 41-year-old mother of two and a trained teacher, founded Berkhampstead in her own home, now our Prep building. With her husband, Dr Robin Andrews, no longer able to work, she made the bold decision to convert part of their home into a school. Classrooms were created, the garden became a playground, and on 20th September 1945, Berkhampstead opened its doors to its first 22 pupils - boys aged 3-11 and girls aged 3-18, with fees of just £5 per term.
Mrs Andrews was a talented musician and an inspirational woman, passionate about education, music and nurturing young minds. She firmly believed that a ‘can-do’ attitude is an asset for life, and the school motto she selected, ‘Perseverantia Vincit’ (Perseverance Conquers), remains at the heart of Berkhampstead School and Day Nurseries today.
The school’s early success led to rapid expansion, and Berkhampstead soon moved into the Grade II listed building across the road, originally known as Beechmount, with the other half, Fernbank, opening later.
From its humble beginnings to the thriving, happy school we know today, Berkhampstead has always been a place of warmth, happiness and opportunity, and we are proud to celebrate 80 years of inspiring young minds.
The school continues to grow and evolve, with significant recent developments that reflect our commitment to excellence and innovation. These include the creation of the Andrews Centre, a purpose-built Early Years building designed to give our youngest pupils the best possible start; the addition of a Multi-Use Games Area - which has transformed opportunities for sport - and the opening of two Day Nurseries that provide an all-year-round education for our youngest children.
From 1945 to today, Berkhampstead has remained a place where childhood is cherished, individuality is celebrated, and every child is encouraged to persevere, grow and shine.

Year 4 Timetable 2026-27
From the age of 3, our children benefit from specialist teaching in music, PE and French, and from age 7 (Year 3), every subject is taught by an experienced, specialist teacher.
Subject specialist teaching, rather than the traditional method of being taught by one classroom teacher each year, ensures high-quality, engaging lessons delivered by teachers with deep knowledge and passion – helping children to thrive, build confidence and develop a love of learning from the very start.
Furthermore, our small class sizes - typically around 14 to 20 pupils - mean that every child is known very well, supported and stretched.
The children also benefit from a healthy ratio of teaching assistants, adding an extra layer of care and academic support.
Small Classes and a Holistic Approach
This expert teaching is complemented by our holistic approach to education, where academic rigour sits alongside sport, outdoor learning, drama, music and well-being. It’s a balance that develops the whole child - mind, body and character.

Pastoral Care
“Happy children learn best.” Mrs Andrews, Founder of Berkhampstead School
Pastoral care lies at the heart of everything we do. While families value our strong academic outcomes and track record of scholarships and Grammar School success, it is our focus on well-being that underpins this achievement.
Well-being encompasses physical, emotional, social and mental health. In today’s fast-moving world, children face increasing pressures, and we equip them with the tools to cope with these.
Pupils take part in weekly well-being lessons, including Circle Time and CWB (Citizenship and Well-Being), covering key life skills such as mental health, relationships, e-safety, healthy living and personal development. These are enhanced through initiatives such as Anti-Bullying Week.
A Structured Approach to Pastoral Care
We’re committed to supporting every child, every day. Our pastoral care is built on three layers:
A Culture of Kindness
Our classrooms are inclusive, supportive environments where children feel confident to express themselves. Our dedicated well-being pod offers all children a calm, nurturing space for reflection and support.
Kindness is actively celebrated through Kindness Cups - awarded each half term - alongside other reward systems across the school. Respect, empathy and inclusion are central to our community, and unkind behaviour is never tolerated.
Preparing Children for Life
Our strapline – Small Classes, Happy Children, Excellent Results - reflects our belief that children thrive and learn best when they feel safe, supported and understood.
Assemblies, leadership opportunities and initiatives such as School Council, Eco Committee and the Platinum Award, encourage children to develop confidence, independence and resilience, always guided by our school motto Perseverantia Vincit - perseverance wins.
